column1: # The C syscall layer's system calls: single source of truth for csys/src/sys/*.c,
# Columns: wrapper name, kernel syscall name (__NR_<name> in the Linux UAPI asm/unistd_64.h),
# spec Appendix A.1 area, argument kinds. Argument kinds follow the kernel ABI:
#   i  a register-sized integer or an address passed as an integer   (C long, Rust i64)
#   c  a pointer to memory the kernel reads                          (C const void *, Rust *const c_void)
#   p  a pointer to memory the kernel writes (or reads and writes)   (C void *, Rust *mut c_void)
# Every wrapper returns the raw kernel result: a value, or -errno.
# Optional fifth column, aarch64 (ledger A-3; numbers from the kernel's generic table, UAPI
# asm-generic/unistd.h, as arm64 configures it). csys-gen fails unless it matches the header:
#   =              (or no column) the same kernel call exists there
#   =backwards     present, arguments in CONFIG_CLONE_BACKWARDS order (clone only; checked against
#                  arch/arm64/Kconfig when a kernel header tree is installed)
#   none:<call>    no number there; on aarch64 the wrapper is built on <call>, a call of this table
#                  (written with the aarch64 C layer, ledger A-6; see docs/arch-syscalls.md)
#   none:-         no number and no wrapper (x86-only; the export follows the reference, RL-8)
# NUMA placement for the allocator (D-3.10). Not in spec Appendix A, which lists what glibc
# itself wraps; Liella uses them internally and exports neither.
